one_sentence: Ehrmann and Fratzscher (2004, Journal of Money, Credit and Banking 36(4), pp. 719-737) show that individual S&P 500 stocks react heterogeneously to U.S. monetary policy shocks, with the reaction concentrated in firms with tighter financial constraints and higher Tobin's q.

issues.reason: Stray JSTOR-import artifact: urldate records when a URL was accessed, but the entry carries no url field at all, so urldate is orphaned and meaningless as written. Either drop it or add the corresponding url (e.g. the JSTOR stable link) it was presumably meant to timestamp.

Verified against the paper's actual abstract (matches in substance: heterogeneous stock reaction to US monetary policy shocks, financial constraints, Tobin's q) so it is not mismatched/mixed content, but a full abstract is non-standard clutter in a citation .bib and is a typical unedited JSTOR-export artifact.

issues.reason: Checked for correctness rather than flagged as wrong: this is JSTOR's verbatim publisher string for pre-2007 JMCB volumes, reflecting that Ohio State University Press was the journal's original publisher/copyright holder while Blackwell/Wiley served (and now serves, as Wiley) as the distributing publisher. The volume/issue/year triple confirms this is the right journal record (Vol. 36, No. 4, August 2004), so the bracketed dual-publisher format is idiosyncratic JSTOR styling, not a data error. A publisher field is unconventional for a plain journal-article @article entry generally, so removal is a stylistic option, not a correction.
